extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) prosecuting applications before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on which public USPTO examiner metrics to consult during patent prosecution and how those metrics should influence prosecution strategy (amend, interview, RCE, pre-appeal, appeal, involve supervisor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner’s allowance rate (i.e., allowance vs. abandonments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A high allowance rate indicates the examiner likely has no qualms about allowing applications and may not stubbornly stick to poor rejections — consider taking a more assertive initial position (argue for withdrawal of rejections or offer modest amendments). A low allowance rate suggests the examiner may combine multiple references and be resistant — consider including substantial amendments, anticipate appeals, or involve the examiner’s supervisor/primary examiner. Also compare the examiner’s allowance rate to the art unit’s allowance rate to decide whether to escalate to supervisory personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office Actions Per Patent, RCEs Per Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Rates of office actions per patent and requests for continued examination (RCEs) per patent for the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High office-actions-per-patent and/or high RCEs-per-patent indicate reaching allowability may be challenging and the examiner may combine many references. For such examiners consider substantial amendments, involving supervisory or primary examiners early, or planning an appeal. Also check supervisory/primary examiner metrics to judge whether escalation may be fruitful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview Statistics / Interview Success Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistics on interviews and the interview success rate (the rate that interviews lead to an allowance in the next office action).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A high interview success rate indicates the examiner uses interviews for compact prosecution and may provide amendment suggestions that lead to allowance—be prepared to discuss multiple amendment options to expedite prosecution. If the interview success rate is low, send a substantive interview agenda with proposed amendments to maximize the chance of agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: After-Final Consideration Pilot (AFCP) Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison of the examiner’s final-rejection allowance rate with AFCP requests versus without AFCP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If allowance rates are significantly higher with AFCP, the examiner likely uses the AFCP’s allocated time to find ways to allow applications—consider filing an after-final amendment with an AFCP request before deciding on an RCE or appeal. If rates are similar, the examiner likely handles after-final matters the same regardless of AFCP, and AFCP filing is less likely to change the outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Appeal Statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Rates of allowance and reopening of prosecution when pre-appeals are filed for the examiner/art-unit/panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A high rate of allowance or reopening after pre-appeal suggests the examiner, the SPE, and panel members take pre-appeals seriously and it may be worthwhile to present arguments in a pre-appeal brief. Low rates of allowance/reopening after pre-appeal suggest it may be better to skip pre-appeal and go straight to an appeal brief or pursue another RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal Statistics (Allowance After Appeal)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s rate of allowance after an appeal is filed (how often appeals result in allowance rather than proceeding to PTAB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If allowance after appeal is relatively high, appealing (instead of filing an RCE) may avoid unnecessary claim narrowing. If allowance after appeal is low, the appeal is likely to go to the PTAB — consider client comfort with delay due to PTAB backlog and weigh against filing an RCE to potentially reach agreement earlier. Use allowance and RCEs-per-patent rates together when making the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board Decision Success Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s success rate at the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (how often the examiner’s positions prevail at the board).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A high board-decision success rate may indicate the examiner only takes matters to the board when confident in the examiner’s answer. If you receive a particularly compelling examiner’s answer from such an examiner, consider filing an RCE rather than immediately appealing to the board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison to Art Unit / Supervisory Examiner Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare the assigned examiner’s metrics (allowance rate, office actions/RCEs) to the art unit averages and to supervisory/primary examiner metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner’s allowance rate is significantly lower than the art unit’s, it may be easier to reach agreement with the supervisor or a primary examiner—consider involving them early. Checking supervisory and primary examiner rates helps decide whether escalation or continued negotiation with the assigned examiner is preferable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tendency to Combine Multiple References in Rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner propensity to combine three, four, or even five-plus references in art rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners with low allowance rates or high office-action counts often combine many references; anticipate this by preparing more substantial claim amendments or stronger responses, and consider whether escalation, appeal, or different amendment strategies are warranted.
